description: I am an independent participant from Myanmar interested in Earth science, environmental data, and technology. My project, Earth Trend Explorer, aims to make global environmental trends easier to understand through an interactive dashboard using NASA data. I am excited to learn, explore, and contribute to the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary: Earth Trend Explorer is an interactive web-based platform designed to help people explore and understand long-term changes in Earth's environment. The project uses NASA's GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4) dataset to visualize historical global temperature anomalies from 1880 to 2025. Users can explore temperature trends through interactive charts, a world map, and a 3D Earth globe. The platform connects a web-based frontend with a Python FastAPI backend to retrieve and present NASA climate data. By transforming scientific records into accessible visualizations, Earth Trend Explorer aims to make climate information easier to understand, encourage environmental awareness, and support learning about global climate change. Additional environmental indicators are presented as demonstration features where live data integration is not yet available.
details:
Earth Trend Explorer is an interactive environmental data visualization platform developed to make long-term climate information easier to explore and understand.

The platform features a 3D rotating Earth globe, an interactive world map, and a temperature trend chart. Its connected data source is NASA's GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4), which provides annual global land-ocean temperature anomalies. The dataset covers 1880–2025 and uses the 1951–1980 reference period as its baseline.

The frontend is built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, while the backend uses Python and FastAPI to retrieve NASA temperature data through an API. Three.js is used for 3D Earth visualization, and Leaflet supports interactive map features.

The project aims to help students, educators, and the public explore climate trends through accessible and engaging visualizations. It encourages scientific curiosity and improves awareness of long-term global temperature changes.

The connected temperature dataset represents global averages, not country-level measurements. Other environmental indicators, including CO₂, sea level, Arctic sea ice, and fire hotspots, are demonstration features and are not presented as verified live data.
